annotation.authors_or_issuer: German Law Journal (Cambridge University Press); author affiliated with China University of Political Science and Law
annotation.summary_en: Journal article arguing Chinese accident law cannot accommodate humanoid robot accidents because of hybrid human-algorithm control, machine learning and human-like interaction. It proposes evidentiary processes (black-box recorders, audits), reasonable-person technical standards with safe harbors, manufacturers as least cost avoiders, and behavioral correction and symbolic retribution for victims.
annotation.title_clean: Reconstructing Liability Mechanism for Humanoid Robot Accidents
annotation.title_en: Reconstructing Liability Mechanism for Humanoid Robot Accidents
key_provisions_or_claims: Chinese fault-based accident law is inadequate for hybrid human-algorithm control and machine learning defects.
Ex ante, in situ and ex post evidentiary measures: algorithm filing, event data recorders, third-party audits.
Adopt 'reasonable person' technical standards for algorithms with technical safe harbors.
Designate manufacturers as least cost avoiders without imposing strict liability; use insurance and cost spreading.
Consider behavioral correction and symbolic retribution against robots to meet victims' psychological needs.
